report.title: PIT at PHI: Week 11 Scouting Report
report.summary: PIT visits PHI facing a pass-first offense that is inefficient but leans on short and intermediate throws. The PHI defense blitzes often and keeps a light box, though its third-down and red zone numbers are soft. Plan protection for the blitz, expect heavy pre-snap motion, and confirm injury status before kickoff.

sections.heading: Opponent offense
sections.body: PHI leans on the pass early, dropping back on 58.3% [oc1] of plays over 398 plays [oc2], and almost exclusively on third and long at 95.3% [oc3] over 64 plays [oc4]. Its passing efficiency is poor at -0.1 [oc9] EPA per pass play over 355 plays [oc10], and average depth of target is 7.2 yards [oc13] over 302 attempts [oc14], so the offense lives in short and intermediate throws. M.Lemon takes 18.9% [oc15] of targets over 285 team targets [oc16], with D.Goedert and D.Smith each at 14.4% [oc17]. S.Barkley takes 36.7% [oc18] of designed rushes over 188 runs [oc19]. PHI uses play action on 17.5% [oc20] of dropbacks over 355 dropbacks [oc21] and pre-snap motion on 56.4% [oc22] of plays over 543 plays [oc23]. Designed runs go right 39.2% [oc24] and left 36.0% [oc25]. Expect motion-heavy looks and make PHI earn its early-down throws.

sections.heading: Opponent defense
sections.body: PHI sends five or more rushers on 26.9% [dc1] of dropbacks over 334 plays [dc2], and its pressure proxy is 11.7% [dc4]. On run plays it keeps 6.4 [dc7] defenders in the box over 252 plays [dc8], a light front. PHI ranks 28th [dc11] in EPA allowed per play at 0.08 [dc9] over 586 plays [dc10], and its explosive play rate allowed is 8.9% [dc13], so chunk plays are the main risk. It allows third-down conversion on 40.6% [dc14] over 133 plays [dc15], 18th [dc16] in the league, and touchdowns on 59.4% [dc17] of red zone trips over 32 drives [dc18], tied for 14th [dc19]. That red zone number is the clearest weakness to attack, though the sample is small.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: PHI's kicker J.Elliott has made 7 [kc1] of 8 [kc2] field goals, an 87.5% [kc3] make rate, and is 100.0% [kc4] on 2 [kc5] tries from long range, though that sample is small. PHI's punts net 42.1 yards [kc6] on 49 punts [kc7], and 44.9% [kc8] land deep in opponent territory, so expect PIT to start drives in a tighter field. PIT's kicker has made 79.2% [kc9] of 24 attempts [kc10]. Only 17.6% [kc13] of 34 kickoffs [kc14] are touchbacks, and PHI's kick returners average 20.8 yards [kc15] on 37 returns [kc16], so a deep kick through the end zone is the safer call. PHI's punt coverage allows 7.8 yards per return [kc17] on 29 returns [kc18], so PIT's returners have a fair chance at yardage.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: PHI's latest report lists 7 players [ic1], and WR DeVonta Smith, WR Dontayvion Wicks, LB Jihaad Campbell and CB Jonathan Jones were all listed Out [ic2][ic3][ic4][ic5], with QB Tanner McKee Questionable [ic6]. Smith is the main loss, with 14.4% [ic7] of team targets over 285 team targets [ic8] so far, and Wicks had 11.2% [ic9], so those targets shift to the remaining receivers. Campbell has logged snaps over 7 games [ic11], so PHI's linebacker snaps need a replacement. PIT's only Questionable player is DT Derrick Harmon [ic13]. He has played 37.8% [ic14] of snaps per game over 5 games [ic15], a small sample, so confirm his status before kickoff.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Pressure decides early downs. PHI sends five or more rushers on 26.9% [mc1] of dropbacks over 334 plays [mc2], and PIT's offense has been sacked or hit on 15.7% [mc3] of dropbacks over 350 plays [mc4]. Keep a back in to protect on third and long, where PHI drops back on 95.3% [mc5] of snaps over 64 plays [mc6]. Pre-snap motion on 56.4% [mc7] of plays over 543 plays [mc8] is the disguise problem, so PIT's linebackers should read the play rather than jump the snap. PHI averages 6.4 [mc13] defenders in the box on runs over 252 plays [mc14], so run into it and set the edge on PHI's right, where its own designed runs go 39.2% [mc15] of the time. Finish drives in the red zone, where PHI allows touchdowns on 59.4% [mc17] of trips over 32 drives [mc18]. With Smith (14.4% [mc19] of team targets over 285 team targets [mc20]) and Campbell (82.4% [mc21] of snaps per game) Out, expect Lemon (18.9% [mc22] of targets over 285 targets [mc23]) and Goedert to absorb volume. Check Harmon's status before kickoff.
